ocr.notes: Mostly right; a few clipped line ends and garbled lines in Hogan's reply speech; the Press Banquet item is included but not about Allen.

title.suggested: Allen and Gallagher at Their Training Quarters

summary.suggested: The Daily Missouri Democrat visited Tom Allen, training under Jim Coyne at the Wash Home, and Charley Gallagher before Tuesday's fight. Allen, a gunsmith by trade, said he was in better condition than when he fought McCoole.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'Daily Democrat, Monday Morning, August 16, 1869'. Reprint of the Aug. 15 article (348).

facts.fact: Allen trained at the Wash Home under Jim Coyne for the Gallagher fight, weighing 170 pounds, and said he was in better condition than when he fought McCoole
Allen was a gunsmith by trade and a good workman at the business
Gallagher knocked Allen out of time in the second round of their fight near St. Louis on February 23, 1869
Allen and Blacksmith Dan seconded Jim Elliott against Gallagher at Peach Island, near Detroit; the fight was broken up by the crowd after 21 rounds
Allen said he would drive Gallagher to his 'bloody corner' and doubted the Canadian had the pluck for a good fight
facts.quote: bloody corner ... bloody glad ... bloody pluck ... bloody good fight

notes: Same article as 348 (Sunday edition), consider merging or treating as duplicate. This edition has the headline and reads 'gunsmith by trade' where 348 reads 'gymnast'.
